title: Filter Controller robustness and visual depth audit
purpose: Create a sober audit lane for the Filter Controller before additional visual or dynamic-tag work is implemented.
objective: Convert Guilherme's concerns into code-grounded analysis tasks covering every filter type, editor fragility, preset persistence, layout packing, and test gaps.
scope_boundary: In scope: source inventory, Elementor control contracts, frontend render/CSS/JS contracts, preset persistence, dynamic tag binding, CPT dynamic-source exposure, visual containment, per-filter customization depth, sort separation, and test planning. Out of scope: implementing fixes before audit findings are complete.
entry_condition: TASK-FC-026 is complete and current user feedback identifies visual overflow, fragile editor integration, insufficient per-filter depth, shop-biased defaults, and weak generalization from examples.
exit_condition: TASK-FC-027 through TASK-FC-044 have produced reports with prioritized findings and a follow-up implementation/test plan.
completion_criteria: Every filter type has a dedicated audit task.
Dynamic tag and CPT exposure are analyzed separately from visual styling.
Sort is analyzed as its own module, not as a filter row.
Layout percentage/row-packing behavior is analyzed as a shared layout engine.
The final synthesis separates implementation tasks from test tasks.

phases.title: Protocol and ownership
phases.purpose: Lock the audit method and source ownership map before detailed findings.

phases.title: Cross-cutting contracts
phases.purpose: Audit containment, dynamic binding, CPT exposure, domain neutrality, and layout packing.

phases.title: Per-filter depth
phases.purpose: Audit every filter type for anatomy, control depth, responsive behavior, states, and visual customization gaps.

phases.title: Sort and editor resilience
phases.purpose: Audit sort as a separate module and evaluate Elementor editor version-drift risk.

phases.title: Synthesis
phases.purpose: Create the next implementation plan and test backlog from the audit findings.

acceptance_criteria: The audit does not collapse into a Range-only or Rating-only repair.
Each report includes source paths, current behavior, failure modes, missing controls, and recommended next task type.
Human visual QA boundaries are preserved for nuanced Elementor/editor craft.
verification: validate_task passes for TASK-FC-027 through TASK-FC-044.
A final export or snapshot records the new audit lane.
stop_conditions: An implementation fix starts before the audit protocol and ownership map are complete.
A user example is treated as the entire scope.
Dynamic tag persistence is changed without a preset migration/sanitization analysis.
